title: What are the terms and the value of each expression?
description: Five expressions with plus, minus, times and divide are split into terms, each term is worked out, and the terms are added. The video checks each value by undoing the steps.
teaching_notes: One idea: the sign in front of a term belongs to it, and times and divide stay inside their term. Ask the child to say the terms aloud before working anything out.

video_script.why: The child writes the terms of five expressions, works out each term, and adds the terms, as in the dosa example.
video_script.substitution: Change the numbers and the signs and the method stays the same: cut at plus and minus, work out each term, then add.
video_script.anchor: five expressions in a column on the board, labelled a to e
video_script.payoff_line: Write the terms, work out each term, then add.

final_answer.spoken: twenty nine, thirty eight, fifty, thirty six and minus one hundred and forty two

video_script.design: One idea: cut the expression at the plus and minus signs, work out each term, then add. The five expressions stay in the anchor band; the working band shows the terms and the values. No hard clear.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the five expressions in a column: (a) 28 − 7 + 8, (b) 39 − 2 × 6 + 11, (c) 40 − 10 + 10 + 10, (d) 48 − 10 × 2 + 16 ÷ 2, (e) 6 × 3 − 4 × 8 × 5

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We have five expressions with plus, minus, times and divide.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We must write the terms of each one and find its value.
Which parts are the terms in twenty eight minus seven plus eight?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the expression 39 − 2 × 6 + 11 cut at the minus and the plus; the sign stays with the term; 2 × 6 stays whole

marks.m1: the words terms are the parts that the plus and minus signs cut are written
marks.m2: 39 − 2 × 6 + 11 is cut at the minus and the plus
marks.m3: the minus stays with 2 × 6, which is not cut

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The terms of an expression are the parts that the plus and minus signs cut apart.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A minus sign stays with the term after it.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Times and divide do not cut a term.

marks.m1: the five expressions are copied to the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, these five expressions.

beats.on_screen: To find: the terms of each expression; the value of each expression

marks.m1: the two things to find are written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to write the terms of each expression, and then find its value.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first expression has the terms twenty eight, minus seven, and eight.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty eight minus seven is twenty one, and twenty one plus eight is twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The second has the terms thirty nine, minus two times six, and eleven.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Two times six is twelve.
Thirty nine minus twelve plus eleven is twenty seven plus eleven, which is thirty eight.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the third expression has the terms forty, minus ten, ten and ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Forty minus ten is thirty, and thirty plus ten plus ten is fifty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The fourth has the terms forty eight, minus ten times two, and sixteen divided by two.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Ten times two is twenty, and sixteen divided by two is eight.
Forty eight minus twenty plus eight is twenty eight plus eight, which is thirty six.

marks.m3: 18 − 160 is written, ready to be worked out

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the last expression has only two terms.
They are six times three, and minus four times eight times five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Six times three is eighteen.
Four times eight is thirty two, and thirty two times five is one hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Eighteen minus one hundred and sixty goes below zero by one hundred and forty two.

marks.m1: the five undo lines are written, one for each part
marks.m2: a tick appears beside each line that returns the first term or the first value

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check each value by undoing the steps.
Twenty nine minus eight plus seven is twenty eight, which is right.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirty eight minus eleven plus twelve is thirty nine, which is also right.
The other three expressions return to their start in the same way.

marks.m2: the minus sign in front of 142 is underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Write the terms, work out each term, then add.
The values are twenty nine, thirty eight, fifty, thirty six, and minus one hundred and forty two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Only the last one is below zero.
